title: Sundarar and the madman
hook: a wedding stopped by an old man with a deed: how Shiva claimed Sundarar first, and turned an insult into his first hymn
carry: shiva claims his servant, and calls him friend
tomorrow: a king summons Appar, and he sends a song.

segments.voice: Yesterday began the Tevaram, Shiva praised in Tamil, place by place: a sealed room, and palm leaves eaten by ants.
screen: `THE TEVARAM: SHIVA PRAISED IN TAMIL, PLACE BY PLACE.`

segments.voice: The wedding is under way. The groom is a handsome young man named Arurar, the families are gathered, the rites have begun. Then an old Brahmin pushes through the crowd, holding up a palm-leaf deed. This young man, he announces, is my slave. His grandfather signed him over to me, him and all his line. The groom loses his temper, calls the old man a madman, and tears the deed to pieces. That insult, the story says, is how one of the Tevaram's three singers found his first word.
screen: `A WEDDING UNDER WAY.` → `AN OLD MAN WITH A DEED.` → `YOU MADMAN.`

segments.voice: The Periya Puranam tells it, in paraphrase. The old man isn't put off. That was only a copy, he says; the original is kept in his own town. So the wedding party follows him there, and before the village elders he produces the deed. They compare the handwriting with the grandfather's. It matches. The groom is bound. Then the old man leads them toward the temple, walks inside, and vanishes. It was Shiva. And Shiva speaks to the young man: you called me a madman, so sing of me, and begin with that word. The young man, known ever after as Sundarar, opens his first hymn with it. In paraphrase: madman, wearing the crescent moon in your hair. The name he shouted in anger becomes praise. Here's the teaching. In Tamil Shaivism, grace, arul, comes first: Shiva goes looking for his devotee before the devotee goes looking for him. He didn't wait for good manners; he took the insult and handed it back as a first line. And bhakti lets you stand before God in more than one way. Devotees are called adiyar, the Lord's servants, and Sundarar's calling begins with a deed saying exactly that. Yet the tradition gives him a second title too, the Lord's friend. Servant and friend, in one man, free to talk back. The wedding didn't happen; that's a hard ending for a bride, and the story doesn't hide it.
screen: `THE DEED IS REAL` · `THE OLD MAN WAS SHIVA` · `GRACE COMES FIRST: ARUL` · `SERVANT AND FRIEND`

segments.voice: Bring to mind something you said recently in frustration, a sharp word aimed at a person, at life, or at God, and without scolding yourself, hear it again quietly. Ask what longing is hidden inside it. Then say it again, plainly, the way Tamil bhakti allows: to God, as a friend who can take it. If you pray, let it become the first line of a prayer, the way Sundarar's did.
Tamil Shaivism and the Tevaram. Today, Sundarar, stopped at his own wedding by Shiva in disguise, whose first hymn begins with the insult he shouted: madman. Today's word.
screen: `TAMIL SHAIVISM AND THE TEVARAM — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: Shiva claims his servant, and calls him friend. A shouted word became a first line of praise. Until next time.
